summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Graf worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg from circa 1988 to 1999 and at the University of Munich from circa 1999 to 2014.

Philosopher Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling studied at Bebenhausen, Nürtingen, the Tübinger Stift, and the universities of Tübingen and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena, Würzburg, Erlangen-Nürnberg, Munich, and Berlin, and led the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz and Karl Foy, and later taught Yinke Chen.

Friedrich Zarncke studied linguistics and other fields at the universities of Rostock and Leipzig, learning under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He founded Literarisches Centralblatt für Deutschland and held posts at Rostock and Leipzig, serving as Leipzig's Rektor in 1852.

Friedrich von Adelung, a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology, studied at the University of Leipzig. He held honorary professorships at Kharkiv University and the University of Tartu in 1809, and positions at Vienna (1824) and Utrecht (1825).

Friedrich von Spiegel studied Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological subjects at Erlangen-Nürnberg, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena under Rückert, Kinkel, Lassen, Brockhaus, and Fleischer. He was professor of Oriental languages at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, studying at Amsterdam, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Madras. He held positions at SOAS, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Amsterdam, and as professor at UC Berkeley (1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar who pursued his studies under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen studied philosophy at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1934), Munich (1936–1941), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (circa 1947–1969), alongside visiting professorships at Córdoba, UCLA, Tokyo, and Chicago.

Frédéric Baudry studied linguistics and Indology under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian positions at the Institut agronomique de Versailles and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, served as administrator of Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885), and joined the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1879.

Fu Yan studied at the Royal Naval College from circa 1877 to 1879 and worked in philosophy and Sinology. He held academic posts at Fudan University (circa 1905–1906) and Peking University (circa 1912).
Fuguan Xu worked in philosophy and Sinology, having studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong. He held a post at Tunghai University from circa 1955 to 1969 and taught Tu Weiming.

Fujio Oda studied at Kyushu University from circa 1952 to 1956. Working in the field of history and archaeology, he held academic posts at Fukuoka University from circa 1978 to 1999 and at Beppu University.

Fujio Taniguchi earned a PhD from Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa, also studying under Yusho Miyasaka, Zuiho Yamaguchi, Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Kaiun Shirodate. His work focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology.

Fumihiko Sueki studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura, Yoshiro Tamura, and Kyosho Hayashima. A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, he held posts at Tokyo, Toho Kenkyukai, Nichibunken, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Fumimaro Watanabe studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Hammalawa Saddhatissa and Anthony Kennedy Warder. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Kindai University (1972–1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

Fumio Enomoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University from circa 1980 to 1984 and as a professor at Osaka University from circa 2000 to 2019.

Fumio Masutani studied Buddhist studies and religious studies at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Matsuda works in the fields of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an organizing committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions, attested in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi studied at Otani University, where he earned a doctorate in literature. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology, he served as an associate professor (circa 1993–2001) and professor (circa 2001–2017) at Otani University.
